jwst.summary: JWST/MIRI 15-micron secondary eclipses detected thermal emission from TRAPPIST-1 b; the dayside brightness temperature is consistent with a dark bare rock and argues against a thick atmosphere.

citation.title: Thermal emission from the Earth-sized exoplanet TRAPPIST-1 b using JWST

jwst.summary: MIRI 15-micron eclipses gave a dayside brightness temperature of 380 +/- 31 K, ruling out a thick CO2-rich (Venus-like) atmosphere; a thin atmosphere or bare rock remain possible.

citation.title: No thick carbon dioxide atmosphere on the rocky exoplanet TRAPPIST-1 c

jwst.summary: Adding 12.8-micron eclipses, the two-band data fit either an airless planet with a fresh ultramafic surface or a thick CO2 atmosphere with a haze-driven temperature inversion; broadband photometry alone cannot decide.

citation.title: Combined analysis of the 12.8 and 15 um JWST/MIRI eclipse observations of TRAPPIST-1 b

jwst.summary: MIRI 15-micron phase curve shows a hot dayside and no significant nightside emission, consistent with a dark airless surface; atmospheres thicker than about 1 bar are strongly disfavoured.

citation.title: No thick atmosphere around TRAPPIST-1 b and c from JWST thermal phase curves

jwst.summary: MIRI 15-micron phase curve: TRAPPIST-1 c could be airless with a more reflective surface or have a thin O2-rich atmosphere; atmospheres thicker than about 1 bar are strongly disfavoured.

citation.title: No thick atmosphere around TRAPPIST-1 b and c from JWST thermal phase curves

jwst.summary: A NIRSpec/PRISM transmission spectrum from two transits is flat within about 100-150 ppm after correcting for stellar contamination, ruling out clear hydrogen-rich and many thicker secondary atmospheres; a bare rock or a very thin or hazy atmosphere remain possible.

citation.title: Strict Limits on Potential Secondary Atmospheres on the Temperate Rocky Exo-Earth TRAPPIST-1 d

jwst.summary: Four NIRSpec/PRISM transits rule out cloudy hydrogen-dominated primary atmospheres at better than 3 sigma, but the data cannot yet tell whether TRAPPIST-1 e has a secondary atmosphere; stellar contamination is significant.

citation.title: JWST-TST DREAMS: NIRSpec/PRISM Transmission Spectroscopy of the Habitable Zone Planet TRAPPIST-1 e
